sections.body: A concept page could compare rendering systems that use explicit models to choose practical approximations under real-time constraints. The motion-quality work uses a fitted perceptual model for refresh-rate and resolution selection; ReSTIR uses reservoir sampling and biased or unbiased estimators to trade variance, cost, and correctness; foveated rendering uses perceptual models and taxonomies to organize quality allocation across rendering paradigms.
sections.heading: Section 1

sections.body: The common concept is controlled approximation: each method accelerates rendering by modeling which samples, pixels, regions, or display states matter most. The sources also show that model-driven choices have failure modes, such as poor motion predictability, bias near discontinuities, weak spatiotemporal correlation, or incomplete perceptual metrics.
